name: Cathedral Basilica of St. James
history: The first St. James church was built in 1822-1823 and became Brooklyn's cathedral when the diocese was formed in 1853. A grand new cathedral begun in Fort Greene in 1868 was never finished. The present church was built in 1903 and became the cathedral again in 1972. John Paul II, who visited in 1979, named it a basilica in 1982.
arch: A red-brick Georgian Revival church by George H. Streeton, with a white steeple and clock in the colonial style.
features: The unfinished Fort Greene cathedral of 1868 never rose above 10 to 20 feet.
It was a pro-cathedral from 1896 while the Fort Greene plans were still alive.

look.d: The white Georgian steeple looks more like colonial New England than Gothic Europe.
Its clock faces Jay Street in Downtown Brooklyn.

fun: It is the cathedral of a diocese of over a million Catholics, yet many big ceremonies happen at larger churches because St. James is small.
journal: A modest brick cathedral among the courthouses. Brooklyn's big plans stopped at 20 feet; this one got built.

quiz.q: When did the diocese of Brooklyn begin?
